title: Transition width across depth
takeaway: The figure quantifies how abruptly the model commits to one of two blended concepts, layer by layer, using the width of the alpha-interval over which a component swings from 10% to 90% commitment. That width is large in early layers, falls steeply over roughly layers 21 through 42, and then flattens. The J-space component's width is consistently somewhat narrower than the non-J-space remainder's and reaches its floor earlier, which is a difference of degree rather than a dissociation.
walkthrough:
The plot turns the [[ignition]]-like behaviour seen earlier into a single number per layer, and then tracks that number across the model's depth.

The horizontal axis runs over the 25 sampled layers of the [[residual-stream]], reindexed to 0-100 so that a layer number reads as a percentage of depth ([[layer-percentage-indexing]]). The vertical axis carries the [[transition-width]]: the change in $\alpha$ needed for a component's [[projection-share]] to go from 10% to 90%. Two series are drawn, each a median across trials with an interquartile band around it. The printed article carries no axis values, so only the shape of the curves is available here.

Both axes rest on the [[embedding-mixture-experiment]]. A concept token's input embedding is replaced by the mixture $(1-\alpha)\,e_B + \alpha\,e_A$ inside an ordinary carrier sentence, and $\alpha$ is swept from 0 to 1. The projection share records where the resulting [[activations]] sit on the line joining that same trial's pure-$B$ activation to its pure-$A$ activation, so it is 0 at one end of the sweep and 1 at the other. Sixteen country-name pairs and forty carrier sentences give 640 trials, and the median and band are taken across them.

The width is a sharpness measure read in reverse. A component whose share simply tracked the input mixture would reach 0.1 at $\alpha = 0.1$ and 0.9 at $\alpha = 0.9$, a width of 0.8. A component that flipped at a threshold would give a width near 0. Smaller is sharper.

The two series split the activation in two ([[j-space-component]]). One is its component along the two concepts' [[j-lens-vector]]s, that is, its content inside the [[j-space]]. The other is the complement left after the top sixteen J-lens vectors are projected out at that position.

Both start wide. Both narrow, steeply over roughly layers 21 through 42, and then settle. The workspace onset that section 4.1 places at layer 38 ([[workspace-layers]]) sits inside that fall.

The claim drawn from the figure is modest. The J-space transition is described as consistently somewhat narrower, and as reaching its floor earlier. The non-J-space activation sharpens too, only later.

terms.definition: The vertical axis quantity: the change in the mixing coefficient needed for a component's projection share to rise from 10% to 90%. It is the paper's scalar measure of how abruptly the model switches from one concept to the other.

The interpolation coefficient of the ambiguous-input experiment, sweeping from 0 (pure concept B in the input embedding) to 1 (pure concept A). Elsewhere in the paper the same letter denotes a steering strength; here it means only the input mixture.

Where an activation sits on the straight line joining that same trial's pure-B activation to its pure-A activation, at the same token position and layer. It is 0 at one end of the alpha sweep and 1 at the other by construction, so it needs no separate calibration.
Depth through the model, reported on 25 evenly spaced residual-stream layers reindexed to the range 0-100 so that a layer number reads as a percentage of total depth.
One of the two series: the part of the activation lying along the two concepts' J-lens directions. This is the content the paper treats as verbalizable workspace content.

The other series: what remains of the activation after the top sixteen J-lens vectors are projected out at each token position. It serves as the control against which the J-space component's sharpness is compared.

One vector per vocabulary token per layer, the direction in residual-stream space that disposes the model to say that token. The two concepts' J-lens vectors define the subspace in which the J-space series is measured.

The region of activation space spanned by sparse non-negative combinations of J-lens vectors, which the paper argues functions as a global workspace. The figure asks whether commitment sharpens faster inside it than outside it.
The line drawn for each series: the middle transition width across the 640 trials at that layer. A median rather than a mean, because individual trials can produce very wide or degenerate widths.

The shaded region around each median, running from the 25th to the 75th percentile of transition widths across trials at that layer. It shows the spread across prompts, not a confidence interval on the median.
The input embeddings of the two single-token concept names being blended, for example two country names. The mixed token's embedding is set to $(1-\alpha)e_B + \alpha e_A$.
In global workspace theory, the late all-or-none amplification of one interpretation of an ambiguous input. A narrow transition width is the paper's operational analogue of it.
The layer at which section 4.1's lens-derived metrics say the J-space starts carrying persistent abstract content, placed at about layer 38. The figure's steep fall brackets it.
The model these results are reported on by default. Key results elsewhere in the paper are corroborated on Haiku 4.5 and Opus 4.5.

numbers.meaning: The figure's number in the appendix section 10.15, Ignition Details. The article prints no caption of its own for it, so the caption shown is inferred from the sentence that introduces it.

The two projection-share levels between which the width is measured. Endpoints nearer 0 and 1 were presumably avoided because the share is pinned exactly to 0 and 1 at the ends of the sweep by construction, which makes the extreme tails uninformative.

The transition width a purely proportional response would give: a share of 0.1 at alpha 0.1 and 0.9 at alpha 0.9 leaves an interval of 0.9 minus 0.1. This value is not stated in the paper; it is the arithmetic anchor for reading the axis, with a step-like response giving a width near 0 instead.
The endpoints of the alpha sweep, and equally the projection share's values at those endpoints. At alpha 0 the input embedding is pure concept B; at alpha 1 it is pure concept A.
The number of top J-lens vectors removed from the activation at each token position to form the non-J-space complement. The paper does not say why sixteen rather than another cut.
The number of pairs of single-token country names used as the two concepts being blended. A separate quantity from the sixteen vectors projected out, despite the shared value.

The number of ordinary carrier sentences into which the mixed embedding is inserted, such as "My sister has always wanted to visit ___". Varying the sentence tests that the effect is not an artifact of one context.

Sixteen concept pairs times forty carrier sentences: the number of trials over which the median and interquartile band at each layer are computed. The paper gives the two factors rather than the product.

The layer range, in the 0-100 percentage-of-depth indexing, over which the paper says the width falls steeply for both components. Before it the width is large; after it both curves are near their floor.
The workspace onset layer identified independently in section 4.1 by lens-derived metrics. It falls inside the 21-to-42 window, which is the alignment the appendix is pointing at.

The layer at which section 4.1 places the end of the workspace band and the start of the motor layers. It bounds the region in which the flattened widths sit, though this figure itself does not mark it.
The depth at which section 10.15 says the sharpness emerges, phrased as about a third of the way through the model. It is a coarser statement of the same transition as the 21-to-42 range.

The number of evenly spaced residual-stream layers sampled throughout the paper, which sets the horizontal resolution of the plot. Section 4.1 notes that layer subsampling can exaggerate how sharp a layerwise transition looks.
The range the sampled layers are reindexed to, so that a layer label reads directly as a percentage of the model's depth rather than as a raw layer count.
The bounds of the interquartile band around each median curve. The paper states only "interquartile band", which is what those quartiles are.

The J-lens rank cut used in Figure 29C, the panel whose measurement this figure quantifies: the J-space projection share is measured only within layers where the two concepts appear in the J-lens top 25. In earlier layers the concepts are absent from the readout, so no J-space share can be formed.
The number of series compared: the J-space component and the non-J-space complement. The whole point of the figure is the gap between them.
